market_holds: Spot $11.92 at the 18:09 UTC seal; Yahoo shows $11.86 intraday on 2026-11-11, against a $20 IPO price and $41.69 at the 52-week high. The stock is down about 48% since the Q2 print ($22.75 on 2026-08-12). The biggest step down was -32.5% on 2026-10-21, on 13.0M shares, after a Bloomberg report that the Navy had stopped buying BlackSea's GARC drone boats. The company denied it the same day. It then fell again with the whole drone group on 11-04 and 11-05 (KTOS -12/-7, RCAT -10/-15, AVAV -8/-10, QQQ -6.5% on 11-05) to a $9.26 close, and bounced about 28% with that group into the print (5-day run-up +14.8%). The front 11-20 straddle is 14.68% at an ATM IV of 104.7%. My own variance split, assuming 70% ordinary vol, puts the event's expected absolute move near 10%. The baseline's 0% event figure is an artefact of the 167% 20-day realised vol, which includes the crash. Calls are bid over puts (25-delta skew -15.9 vol points) and put/call open interest is 0.91, so the upside is the side being paid for; Stocktwits sentiment was 'extremely bullish' after the crash. Q3 consensus is about $150.8M revenue and $0.09 EPS (Earnings Whispers preview, 2026-11-03). FY26 consensus is about $760M (TIKR) to $764M (Oppenheimer, 10-22); that is the $700-720M guide, which excludes BlackSea, plus roughly four months of BlackSea at a $150M annual rate. For 2027, Oppenheimer has $834M and TIKR consensus implies about +20% (~$910M). Both figures predate or straddle the GARC report and have not been cut. Targets cluster at $13 (Piper Sandler Neutral, UBS) up to $21-26 (RBC $22, Jefferies $26, Oppenheimer $21). Management said on the Q2 call that Q3 is the smallest quarter of 2026 and that most Deep Strike revenue rolls off this year. Prior reactions: Q1 (05-20) +1.7%; Q2 beat-and-raise opened -5% and closed -8%. Short interest was 3.5M at 06-30 and about 3.8M at the 09-30 settlement (as % of float: not available).
view: This print turns on 2027, not on Q3. Q3 itself should land near consensus. About 95% of the FY revenue midpoint was in backlog in August, management already told the Street Q3 is the trough quarter, and about three weeks of BlackSea (~$9-10M at a $150M rate) lands on top of roughly $135-140M organic, which is close to the $150.8M consensus. The headline numbers will mostly look benign: funded backlog should rise from $259.8M because BlackSea's ~$110M of funded backlog comes in, the FY guide should rise mechanically to include BlackSea, and the company will likely quantify GARC's share of BlackSea to rebut the Bloomberg report. The danger is the gap between sell-side 2027 numbers and the arithmetic. From the 10-Q, Deep Strike was about $228M of H1 revenue; with the H2 remainder it is about $300M+ of 2026, leaving roughly $400M of 2026 revenue that is not Deep Strike. Getting to $834-910M in 2027 with only 'a little bit' of Deep Strike left (CFO, Q2 call) needs about $150M of BlackSea plus 60%+ growth in everything else, or a Deep Strike successor. Announced awards since June (the $88.1M strike order, $41M one-way attack, up to $92.2M SkyRange, $41.6M mine-countermeasure, plus smaller ones) are real but nowhere near that. So if management gives a 2027 framework it is more likely below the sell side than above it, and Kratos's 11-05 reaction (beat, then -10.6% on a 2027 guide below consensus) shows how this group trades that. Against that, a $12 stock with Piper and UBS at $13 already holds most of the bear case, and NTM P/E is about 17-20x on estimates that have not been cut. An in-line quarter, a guide raised for BlackSea, a sized GARC rebuttal and vague '2027 growth' language could squeeze a crowd that is retail-long and sector-beaten. I lean slightly down, about 45/55, nowhere near a bet.
unpriced: Possibly the 2027 revenue gap: sell-side 2027 numbers ($834M Oppenheimer, ~$910M implied by TIKR) appear to need either a Deep Strike follow-on or 60%+ growth outside Deep Strike, and nothing public shows that. But the share price (~$12, at the bearish targets) already looks closer to my arithmetic than the published estimates do, so the gap is between the estimates and reality, not clearly between the price and reality. And management may not give a 2027 number on this call. Not a recommendable mispricing.

recommendation.reason: The decisive line is the 2027 framework. My rebuild from the 10-Q (Deep Strike ~$300M+ of 2026 revenue rolling off) says the sell side's 2027 numbers are too high. But the price has already fallen about 48% to near the bearish $13 targets, and whether management quantifies 2027 on this call is uncertain. Retail-long positioning and a sector that has just rebounded add noise that can swamp the signal overnight. Direction confidence is about 55%, below the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A stated 2027 outlook at or above roughly $830M, or a large disclosed Deep Strike follow-on or new strike-drone production award, together with GARC sized as a small share of BlackSea. That would point clearly up. A 2027 framework near flat-to-down from pro forma 2026 would make it a clear down.

self_critique: The strongest case against a down lean: the stock has already priced a 2027 disappointment. It trades at the lowest sell-side targets and has been cut in half; a printed beat, a guide raised for BlackSea, backlog up sharply and a sized GARC rebuttal would read as 'less bad', and retail and call buyers are positioned for a squeeze in a sector that just bounced. Management also controls whether a 2027 number comes out at all, and an IPO-year team with a class action pending has every reason to talk up the pipeline ($10.5B) rather than guide low. My Deep Strike arithmetic may also overstate the cliff if part of the $88.1M strike order and the $41M one-way-attack order are successor production. That is why I stay at 45, not lower.
